outcome: SARS-CoV-2 detection in newborn's nasopharyngeal swabs
cohort: The study enrolled 56 SARS-CoV-2-positive pregnant women, with 82% in their third trimester of pregnancy.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 was detected in 27% of rectal swabs but not in vaginal swabs of pregnant women in the third trimester, and no virus was detected in newborn's nasopharyngeal swabs, suggesting intrapartum vaginal or orofecal SARS-CoV-2 transmission is unlikely.
mod_finding: No virus particles were detected in vaginal swabs of SARS-CoV-2 positive pregnant women, suggesting intrapartum vaginal SARS-CoV-2 transmission during vaginal delivery is unlikely.
cross-section timing: Intrapartum, with most women in their third trimester of pregnancy.
gest_age: Most participants (82%) were in the third trimester, 10% in the second, and 7% in the first trimester of pregnancy.
